topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: It's only ten o'clock, and I ___ three cups of coffee this morning. (drink)
correct answer: have drunk | 've drunk | have had | 've had
explanation shown to learner: *this morning* is still going on (it's ten o'clock): present perfect, *I've drunk*.
explanation in Latvian: *this morning* vēl turpinās (ir desmit no rīta): Present Perfect, *I've drunk.*
replaces: It's only eleven, and I ___ the bank four times. Nobody answers. (ring)

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: It's six in the evening now. I ___ much this morning because the internet was down. (not / do)
explanation shown to learner: The morning is over (it's six in the evening): past simple, *I didn't do much this morning*.
explanation in Latvian: Rīts ir beidzies (ir seši vakarā): Past Simple, *I didn't do much this morning.*

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: Choose the correct option: Since she ___ the team, sales have doubled.
explanation shown to learner: *since* + past simple for the point in the past when it started (*since she joined*), present perfect in the main part (*have doubled*).
explanation in Latvian: *since* + Past Simple brīdim pagātnē, kad tas sākās (*since she joined*), Present Perfect galvenajā daļā (*have doubled*).

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: Have you made any friends since you ___ in this city? (live)
correct answer: have lived | 've lived | have been living | 've been living
explanation shown to learner: Both situations go on until now (you still live here): present perfect also after *since*: *since you've lived here*.
explanation in Latvian: *Abas* situācijas turpinās līdz šim brīdim (tu joprojām te dzīvo): Present Perfect arī aiz *since*: *since you've lived here*.
answer notes: have been living :: Also possible: the continuous stresses that the living here still goes on. :: Arī pareizi: Continuous forma uzsver, ka tu te joprojām dzīvo.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: I'll text you the moment I ___ my exam results. (get)
correct answer: 've got | get | have got | 've gotten | have gotten | have received | 've received
explanation shown to learner: *the moment* about the future: present perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) or present simple (*the moment I get my results*), both correct; never *will* or the past.
explanation in Latvian: *the moment* par nākotni: Present Perfect (*the moment I've got my results*) vai Present Simple (*the moment I get my results*), abi pareizi; nevis *will* vai pagātne.
answer notes: get :: Also possible: after *the moment* the present simple has the same meaning. :: Arī pareizi: aiz *the moment* Present Simple nozīmē to pašu.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
correct answer: Once you paid, the order can't be changed.
wrong options / checks: The moment we landed, I texted her. | After she had left hospital, she went on a long holiday. | I'll call you as soon as I've finished.
explanation shown to learner: *Once* about something that has not happened yet (*the order can't be changed*): present perfect or present simple, *Once you've paid*. *The moment we landed* is about the past, so the past simple is right there.
explanation in Latvian: *Once* par to, kas vēl nav noticis (*the order can't be changed*): Present Perfect vai Present Simple, *Once you've paid.* *The moment we landed* ir par pagātni, tāpēc tur Past Simple ir pareizi.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: This is the third time she ___ her keys this week! (lose)
explanation shown to learner: *This is the first / second / third time* + present perfect: *she has lost her keys*.
explanation in Latvian: *This is the first / second / third time* + Present Perfect: *she has lost her keys*.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
correct answer: This is the first time I am seeing snow.
wrong options / checks: It was the first time I'd been on a plane. | It's the second time he has missed the train this month. | It won't be the first time they've voted against the plan.
explanation shown to learner: After *This is the first time*, the present perfect: *This is the first time I've seen snow.* After *It was the first time*, the past perfect.
explanation in Latvian: Aiz *This is the first time* lieto Present Perfect: *This is the first time I've seen snow.* Aiz *It was the first time* lieto Past Perfect.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: It's only eleven, and I ___ the bank four times. Nobody's answering. (ring)
explanation shown to learner: A number of times (*four times*): present perfect simple, *I've rung*. The continuous is for the activity: *I've been ringing all morning*.
explanation in Latvian: Reižu skaits (*four times*): Present Perfect Simple, *I've rung.* Continuous forma ir darbībai: *I've been ringing all morning.*

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
correct answer: I've been having this phone since May.
wrong options / checks: Rents have gone up by eight per cent this year. | She's been learning Spanish for two years. | We've been waiting for the plumber since nine.
explanation shown to learner: *have* meaning *own* is a state: present perfect simple, *I've had this phone since May*.
explanation in Latvian: *have* nozīmē piederēt ir stāvoklis: Present Perfect Simple, *I've had this phone since May.*

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: By next May I ___ at this school for ten years. (teach)
correct answer: will have taught | 'll have taught | will have been teaching | 'll have been teaching
explanation shown to learner: Up to a point in the future (*by next May*): future perfect, *I'll have taught* or *I'll have been teaching*.
explanation in Latvian: Līdz brīdim nākotnē (*by next May*): Future Perfect, *I'll have taught* vai *I'll have been teaching.*
answer notes: will have been teaching :: Also possible: the continuous stresses the teaching as an activity that goes on. :: Arī pareizi: Continuous forma uzsver mācīšanu kā darbību, kas turpinās.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: The thief is thought ___ the country last week. (leave)
explanation shown to learner: *is thought* is now, the leaving was earlier (*last week*): the perfect after *to*, *to have left*.
explanation in Latvian: *is thought* ir tagad, aizbraukšana bija agrāk (*last week*): perfekts aiz to, *to have left*.

topic: The perfect tenses: forms and uses
task: Report what she said with *deny* and *having*. Her words: 'I didn't read the letter.'
correct answer: She denied having read the letter. | She denied reading the letter.
explanation shown to learner: *deny* + *having* + 3rd form for something earlier than the denying: *She denied having read the letter.* (*She denied reading the letter* is natural too.)
explanation in Latvian: *deny + having* + 3. forma tam, kas notika pirms noliegšanas: *She denied having read the letter.* (*Dabiski* ir arī *She denied reading the letter*.)
answer notes: She denied reading the letter. :: Also correct and natural; the task asks for *having*, which shows that the reading came first. :: Arī pareizi un dabiski; uzdevums prasa *having*, kas parāda, ka lasīšana bija agrāk.
